out_data_not_delivered_14 is rejected because it is categorized as data and was not delivered by Operator. The stated exclusion is limited to data delivered to Owner; the broad included term "materials" is not implemented faithfully by a categorical data exclusion.

The source defines the contractual term "Territory," but the predicate instead evaluates a distinct field, "jurisdiction." The source does not state that applicable jurisdiction determines Territory, so this substitution is not an exact implementation.
The cases in_usa_territory and in_canada_territory state facts about the relevant territory but code those facts as jurisdiction; their coded field is not explicitly stated in the case text.

The source gives no basis for treating jurisdictions outside the United States and Canada as a defined exhaustive value universe, although testing them as nonmembers would be acceptable only after correcting the field to Territory.

The source says systems 'for vehicles and trailers.' The proposed predicate substitutes an inclusive OR condition ('for vehicles or trailers'). This is a plausible commercial reading but is not an exact logical consequence of the quoted conjunction; the source does not resolve whether both vehicle and trailer use is required or whether the phrase names alternative categories.
The source is insufficient to validate the proposed OR predicate exactly without a definition, surrounding contract language, or other authoritative clarification of 'for vehicles and trailers.'
Case in_vehicle_unspecified_trailer expressly leaves trailer compatibility unspecified but codes is_for_trailers=false.
Case in_trailer_unspecified_vehicle expressly leaves vehicle compatibility unspecified but codes is_for_vehicles=false.
Cases out_not_refrigeration and out_vehicle_but_not_refrigeration do not expressly state that the systems are not for trailers, although is_for_trailers=false is coded.
Case out_trailer_but_not_refrigeration does not expressly state that the system is not for vehicles, although is_for_vehicles=false is coded.

The predicate improperly requires that every controversy or claim be based on one of the enumerated legal/equitable theories. The source uses the inclusive phrase "whether based on contract, tort, statute or other legal or equitable theory" and does not make that disjunction an additional stated eligibility condition for every controversy or claim.
The predicate and summary do not expressly preserve that "this Agreement" includes amendments or extensions; the source expressly includes them.

c05 states that the claim concerns termination of the Agreement and post-termination obligations, but codes arises_out_of_or_relates_to_agreement as false. It also does not expressly state that the declaration claim is based on contract, despite coding basis_contract as true.
c09 does not state that the dissatisfaction concerns the Agreement or is contract-based, but codes arises_out_of_or_relates_to_agreement and basis_contract as true.

The actual Agreement and any amendments/extensions are not provided. Those materials are identified as dependencies and may be necessary to determine whether a matter relates to the Agreement or concerns its breach or termination where the case text does not conclusively supply that fact.

The source defines Effective Date solely as "the date of last signature on this Agreement." The added field is_signature_date_on_this_agreement is not an independent stated condition. Although ordinarily entailed by being the date of the last signature on the Agreement, making it a separately required Boolean condition permits outcomes that the source rule does not permit if the fields differ.

Case out_not_on_agreement does not support its coded value is_date_of_last_signature_on_agreement=true. Its text says the candidate is the last-signature date but expressly says that signature is not on this Agreement; it therefore cannot explicitly establish that the candidate is the date of the last signature on this Agreement. The stated facts conflict with, or at minimum fail to establish, the coded vector.

The predicate should directly test only whether the candidate date is the date of the last signature on this Agreement. Any signature-date concept is inherent in that phrase and should not be a separate eligibility gate.

The predicate treats `other_entity` as an unrestricted residual entity category. The source instead refers to “other law, rule or regulation-making organizations or entities”; it does not extend coverage to every other kind of entity that has jurisdiction or exercises authority. Thus, for example, a non-law/rule/regulation-making private entity with qualifying authority would be included by the proposed predicate but is not expressly included by the definition.

The field/value design should distinguish the specifically covered residual category of other law-, rule-, or regulation-making organizations/entities from entities outside the enumerated and residual covered categories. The existing `other_entity` value is overbroad.

The membership predicate faithfully tracks the quoted definitional clause: qualifying entity type, acquisition of Services from Channel Partner, and use by the entity's employees and contractors are all required. The separate no-resale sentence is a restriction on Business Entities, not an additional criterion for becoming one.

The definitions of the capitalized terms "Services" and "Channel Partner" are identified as dependencies but are not supplied. Their absence prevents a complete audit of the incorporated contractual meaning and of whether the case descriptions actually satisfy those defined terms.

Several purported nonqualifying entity-type scenarios rely on an unstated exclusivity assumption. A limited liability company, sole proprietorship, or nonprofit organization is not expressly stated to be outside the contractual category "corporation, partnership, or enterprise"; in particular, a nonprofit may be a corporation and "enterprise" may have a defined or broader meaning. This does not contradict the coded fact text, but it limits the cases' ability to establish exclusion without the missing definitions or express negative facts.
The predicate exactly captures the four conjunctive requirements stated in Section 1.2; 'published or made available' is correctly represented by a single affirmative field.

The source is insufficient to fully operationalize the incorporated terms: the Customer definition in Section 1.1, Licensed Product definition in Section 1.4, and Exhibit A are absent. The Licensor identity and Agreement term are also not supplied.
Each case text expressly states the coded value for every predicate field; no case-specific fact vector is unsupported by its text.
The predicate faithfully captures the quoted definition as a conjunction: information, written or other tangible form, specifically labeled as Confidential Information, and disclosed by a Party.

Every case codes is_information=true, but none expressly states that the disclosed item is 'information.' Describing an item as a report, memo, statement, prototype, disk, or draft is not an express stipulation of that coded fact; in particular, a tangible prototype or disk need not itself be information without further facts.

The definition of the capitalized term 'Party' is identified as required but is not supplied. Therefore the source record is insufficient to determine Party status independently of the case assertions.

The stated dependencies also refer to definitions of Agreement and Service, but neither definition is provided; Service does not appear in the quoted rule, while the missing Party definition is material.

The predicate faithfully encodes the quoted Redistributor definition as a conjunction of individual-or-entity status, a grant by Licensee, and authority to copy and sublicense one or more Licensed Products to Customers.
Each case text expressly supports its coded positive and negative scope/grant facts.

Definitions or source materials for the referenced defined terms "Licensee," "Licensed Products," and "Customers" are not provided. The program identifies these dependencies, but the supplied source is insufficient to verify their underlying contractual meaning or any qualifications contained in those definitions.
The predicate faithfully implements the quoted definition: a Copyright is a copyright or copyright application, excluding Trademarks.
The definition of the capitalized dependent term "Trademarks" is not supplied. Its scope cannot be verified from the provided source quote alone.
c01, c02, c04, and c05 code is_copyright_application=false, but their texts do not expressly state that no copyright application exists.
c03 and c06 code is_copyright=false and is_registered=false. A pending copyright application does not expressly state either coded negative fact.
c11 and c12 code is_copyright=false, but a registered copyright application does not expressly state that it is not also a copyright.
c13 and c14 code is_copyright=false, but an unregistered copyright application does not expressly state that it is not also a copyright.

The source does not establish that registration status applies to copyright applications; although is_registered is not used by the predicate, application-registration case characterizations are unsupported by the quoted text.

The subsequent-Contract-Year branch is not an exact transcription of the source. The source defines subsequent Contract Years as 'the successive twelve (12) month period thereafter'; it does not expressly require a period to 'start immediately after a prior Contract Year.'

The predicate introduces the distinct and stronger concepts of 'immediately' and a 'prior Contract Year.' Those may be a plausible interpretation of 'successive ... thereafter,' but they are not stated in the quoted definition and therefore should not be substituted in an exact-rule program.

The first-Contract-Year branch is faithfully represented by commencement on the Effective Date and ending one year thereafter. All case fact vectors are explicitly stated in their respective fact text.

The source defines two coordinated categories: (1) normative documents related to the platform and noticed to Party B by Party A by E-mail or other means, and (2) various normative documents published on the platform. The proposed predicate incorrectly requires platform-relatedness for the publication category as well.

Accordingly, a normative document that is not stated to be related to the platform but is published on the platform is excluded by the proposed predicate, although it falls within the separately stated published-documents category.

The referenced Definition of Platform (1.1) is not supplied. That external definition is required to operationalize the terms 'platform,' 'related to the platform,' and 'published on the platform' with contractual precision.
The quoted definition relies on the capitalized defined term "Country," but its definition is not provided. This external definition may delimit which governments and political subdivisions qualify.

The political-subdivision field value must be understood as a subdivision of a government of a qualifying Country, as required by "thereof" in the source. The supplied case texts do state a Country, but this relationship is not independently represented in the predicate fields.

The definition covers specifically enumerated classes: governments; governmental, regulatory, or administrative authorities; agencies; commissions; courts; tribunals; and judicial or arbitral bodies. The independent is_governmental predicate is not an exact implementation because it can include an entity that is merely described as governmental without establishing that it is a governmental authority. Case c20 illustrates this ambiguity: a private company being 'governmental' does not necessarily establish that it is a governmental authority under the quoted definition.

The fields is_governmental and is_judicial_or_arbitral are redundant with, and less precise than, the enumerated entity classifications. Their use permits classifications not expressly limited to an authority or body, respectively, and therefore is not a conservative exact translation of the source.

Cases c01 through c20 code at least one negative Boolean fact (is_governmental:false and/or is_judicial_or_arbitral:false) that is not explicitly stated in their fact text. A statement that an entity is, for example, a court or a private company does not expressly state the negative values of both other fields.

Several negative Boolean codings are particularly difficult to reconcile with the stated field meanings: courts, tribunals, judicial bodies, arbitral bodies, and arbitration panels are coded is_judicial_or_arbitral:false despite their fact text expressly identifying judicial/arbitral-type entities. Even if entity_type independently triggers the result, the case vectors do not faithfully state all coded facts.
The source quote itself is sufficient to define the term; no external attachment or redacted contractual provision is required for the basic enumerated-class rule.

The predicate's four alternative inclusion branches enumerate every possible combination of in_consultant_possession_or_control_on_effective_date and developed_in_performance_of_services. That disjunction is tautological, so the predicate reduces to information/materials/methods that were not made available by Aduro to the general public. It does not implement the source's possession/control-on-Effective-Date or developed-in-performance qualification, and contradicts the program's own rule summary.

The public-domain exclusion is incomplete. The source excludes information that is public at disclosure or becomes public after disclosure, through no improper act by Consultant or any of its employees. The program contains only an at-time-of-disclosure field and omits the after-disclosure pathway.
The improper-act field and case language cover only an act by Consultant, omitting improper acts by Consultant's employees specified in the source.

The program omits the source's specific-information qualification: information is not public-domain or prior-possession information merely because it is encompassed or contemplated by more general public-domain or prior-possession information.

Every case includes coded boolean facts that its fact text does not expressly state. Common examples include acquired_directly_or_indirectly_from_work_with_aduro=false, possession_shown_by_written_evidence=false, and third_party_obtained_directly_or_indirectly_from_aduro=false where the case merely says there was no third-party receipt or no prior possession. A fact being irrelevant under a particular scenario does not make an unstated coded value textually supported.
The source quote itself is sufficient and contains no apparent redaction or required external attachment, but the proposed field schema is insufficient to encode all operative source distinctions.
The predicate does not implement the contractual interval. It ignores both agreement_date and certification_date and instead hard-codes a fixed set of calendar dates.

The source says the period commences on the Agreement date; cases in_early, in_april, out_before_start, and out_early demonstrate that the predicate can return true for an evaluation date preceding the Agreement date.

The source ends the period at 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time on the certification date. That endpoint includes times on the certification date through 11:59 p.m.; the predicate categorically excludes the entire certification date.

Cases whose evaluation_date equals certification_date do not state an evaluation time. They therefore cannot be conclusively classified under a rule with an 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time endpoint. The program's asserted full-day exclusion is unsupported.

The rule_summary conflicts with the predicate: the summary says the period runs from the Agreement date through the certification date, while the predicate excludes the certification date and does not use the Agreement date.

The source definition is self-contained and supplies the governing rule, but a faithful executable representation needs comparison operators and, for certification-date cases, an evaluation timestamp or an explicit date-granularity convention consistent with the 11:59 p.m. endpoint.

The predicate is not the source definition. The source defines an Affiliate as an entity that controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with a Party. The program instead requires a Party or an entity already under common control with a Party to control a separate Entity B, without identifying which entity is being classified.
The source expressly includes the direction where the candidate entity is controlled by a Party. The predicate has no branch for that relationship.

The source's common-control branch applies directly to an entity under common control with a Party. The program requires that entity additionally control Entity B and classifies an unstated target, which changes the rule.
Control by ownership is 'at least' 50%; the predicate enumerates only 50, 51, and 100. It incorrectly excludes valid percentages such as 52%, 60%, 75%, and 99%.
The source requires beneficial ownership. The program uses ownership generally and omits the beneficial-ownership qualification.

The source covers control directly or indirectly and at present or in the future. The program does not faithfully represent the temporal qualification and uses an unscoped direct_or_indirect_control field rather than the required relationship between the candidate entity and the Party.

The fields and case texts do not consistently identify the entity to which each fact applies. In particular, has_effective_power_to_appoint_or_dismiss_management is coded true based on Entity A holding the power in the power cases, but coded false based on Entity B lacking power in the other cases.

In ownership cases, direct_or_indirect_control is coded true although the fact text only expressly states ownership; it does not expressly state the separately coded control fact. Under the requested explicit-fact standard, this is an inferred rather than stated field value.
The common-control field is likewise scoped to Entity A in the prose, while other coded facts variously concern Entity A or Entity B. An unscoped vector cannot exactly encode the source relationship.
All cases are fatally unsuitable for validating the stated predicate because the candidate Affiliate, Party, and controlled/common-controlled entity are not consistently represented.

The public-availability exclusion is not modeled exactly. The source requires that the information be generally available other than as a result of disclosure by 'such party'—the receiving party. The proposed field and predicate instead use generic 'party disclosure,' losing the identity of the receiving party and potentially changing the exclusion's result.

The Section 7 attachment is absent. The definition expressly conditions treatment of the Agreement-existence fact on what is specifically permitted in Section 7, so the asserted Section 7 facts and the exact operation of that exception cannot be audited from the supplied source quote alone.

Case out_public_availability does not expressly establish the source-required receiving-party-specific qualification. It says availability was other than through disclosure 'by a party,' and Pi is not expressly identified as the receiving party or as the relevant party whose disclosure is excluded.

Several public-availability case narratives similarly refer to disclosure by the disclosing party or by an unspecified party rather than specifically by the receiving party. This may not affect their coded false values in every case, but it does not support an exact implementation of source item (z).

The source defines Users as subscribers to Licensee's services. The proposed predicate adds a separately coded requirement that the person be a 'subscriber' in addition to subscribing to Licensee's services. The supplied quote does not establish that these are independent required conditions rather than that 'subscriber to Licensee's services' is a single relationship; this conjunction is therefore not an exact transcription of the source.

The program identifies required dependencies (the definitions/scope of Licensee, Licensee's services, and subscriber), but none of those attachments or definitions are supplied. Their absence prevents validating the intended scope and whether the two proposed fields are distinct.

Each case's stated facts are explicitly reflected in its fact vector, notwithstanding misleading case IDs such as 'in_subscriber_only_true' and 'in_services_only_true,' whose text and vectors both state both facts are true.

The source says a Web site 'of the Customer'; the program substitutes the narrower and non-equivalent condition 'owned_by_customer.' Ownership is not expressly required by the quoted definition, so the predicate is not an exact rendering.

The two cases excluded solely because the site is not owned by Customer assume that lack of ownership means the site is not 'of the Customer.' The source does not state that implication; a Customer site could be operated, controlled, or otherwise be 'of' Customer without Customer owning it.

The quoted source incorporates the terms and conditions of the Agreement, but the Agreement and any definition or allocation establishing what constitutes a Customer Web site or hosting under the Agreement are absent. The cases stipulate the hosting facts, but the external contract context needed to validate the ownership-based substitution is unavailable.
The predicate is not an interval-membership rule: it merely whitelists five test dates and does not compare test_date to the applicable Program Year's start and end dates.

The predicate ignores start_year and end_year entirely. Consequently, it returns true for dates that are listed globally but fall outside the Program Year described in a case, including out_2024_10_01, out_2025_09_30, and out_2023_10_01.

The source expressly includes 'such shorter period' when a particular Program Year starts or ends in the middle of the Program Year. The proposed predicate instead categorically excludes every shorter period.

The shorter-period case does not state the actual shortened start and/or end date. Therefore its membership result cannot be determined from the stated facts, and the source excerpt alone does not provide a method for deriving those dates.
The definition does not limit Program Years to 2023-2026 or test dates to an enumerated list; the predicate improperly hard-codes both a narrow date universe and particular calendar dates.
Although the individual coded fact values are explicitly supported by their corresponding case text, the available source and facts are insufficient to implement the shorter-period exception exactly.

The predicate incorrectly requires the candidate Affiliate itself to be a Party. The source instead defines an Affiliate with respect to a particular Party; the candidate need only be a Person having the specified relationship to that Party.

The predicate treats ownership of 50% or more of voting stock, a contractual right, and other means as alternatives to actual power. The source defines control as actual power to direct or cause direction of management and policies, with ownership, contract, or otherwise describing how that power may arise rather than independent substitutes for actual power.
The predicate does not capture the full definition of control: it omits actual power to cause the direction of management and policies, not merely power to direct management.

The case narratives generally identify a named Person as the Party and describe that Party's relationship to another Entity, while the coded relationship fields require an assessed Person's relationship to the reference Party. The other Entity is generally not expressly stated to be a Person or the particular Party, so the required affiliate/reference-party orientation is absent.

Several vectors assert facts not explicitly stated in their case text, including control of a Party and actual/direct management power. This is especially clear in out_less_than_50pct, whose text never says Person W controls Entity X, and out_no_control_relation, whose coded actual-power fact is incompatible with the stated absence of a control relationship under the supplied definition.
The ownership, contract, and 'other means' cases do not expressly establish actual power to direct or cause direction of management and policies, which is required by the source definition.

Definitions of Party and Person are identified as dependencies but are not supplied. The case texts also omit necessary facts establishing which entity is the particular Party and whether the purported affiliate entity is a Person.

The predicate improperly makes recognition under the law of a governmental authority a universal prerequisite for every listed category. In the quoted definition, the phrase 'under the laws of any governmental authority' most directly qualifies 'similar rights of any type,' not trade secrets, patents, copyrights, trademarks, know-how, moral rights, or applications and registrations generally.

Consequently, the proposed program excludes otherwise listed patent, copyright, trade-secret, and qualifying application/registration rights solely because they are coded as not recognized under governmental-authority law, an exclusion not expressly present in the source.

The case texts explicitly state the coded fields they use, and the quoted source is sufficient to identify the overbroad governmental-law condition. However, the source does not support treating that condition as a required fact for all enumerated categories.

The source says the replacement applies "from and after" the time the prospectus is filed with the Commission. This is a strictly post-filing condition and excludes the exact instant of filing. The predicate instead uses an inclusive "at_or_after_filing_time" field and treats the exact filing time as satisfying the exception.
Accordingly, the two exact-time cases are incorrectly admitted by the predicate and rule summary.

The predicate adds registration_statement_initially_effective as an independent Boolean requirement. The source uses the initial-effective-time prospectus as the comparison benchmark; it does not separately state that initial effectiveness is an additional conjunct apart from the stated differing-from-that-prospectus condition.

The cases asserting that the Registration Statement had not initially become effective while also asserting a difference from the prospectus on file at that initial-effective time are internally problematic, because the identified comparison-time prospectus is not coherently established under those stated facts.

The predicate correctly captures the definition: a web site of the Company that is on the Internet. The www.iship.com clause identifies a currently existing example and does not add a predicate condition or exception.

The field is_company_site is redundant and circular: its stated source basis is the defined term itself, while the predicate independently determines that conclusion. It should be removed from case fact vectors or renamed to a non-conclusory underlying fact.

Cases in_basic and in_second_site refer to Acme Corp rather than the contractual Company. Neither case expressly states that Acme Corp is the Company, and no supplied attachment or dependency definition establishes that identity. Their is_web_site_of_company=true coding is therefore unsupported by the stated facts.
The remaining cases generally expressly state, or directly negate, the two operative underlying facts: that the item is a web site of the Company and that it is on the Internet.
The predicate faithfully implements the stated inclusion routes and the five exclusions, including the competent-written-proof requirement and the notice-and-scope proviso for compelled disclosure.

The case fact vectors are not fully text-grounded. Across the cases, numerous fields are coded false although the accompanying fact text does not explicitly state their negation. For example, cases involving a third-party receipt set disclosed_by_party_to_other, oral_or_written_form, and other exclusion-related facts to false without expressly establishing those facts; a third-party receipt does not itself establish that no party-to-party disclosure also occurred or that the information was not oral or written.

Similarly, exclusion-focused cases generally establish one proven exclusion but do not expressly state false values for all other coded exclusion predicates. Statements such as 'no exclusion applies' or inability to demonstrate an exclusion may establish the operative outcome, but do not explicitly establish every underlying raw fact encoded false (for example, that information is not actually public-domain rather than merely unproven).
The source quote itself is sufficient to encode the rule; no required external attachment or redacted contract language is apparent.

The definition identifies a particular Gas Gathering Agreement and includes the conventional updating phrase 'as amended, restated or otherwise modified from time to time.' It does not make the existence of an actual amendment, restatement, or modification a required eligibility condition. The predicate improperly requires amended_restated_or_modified=true.
c05 demonstrates the error: an otherwise identified original agreement does not cease to be the defined Gathering Agreement merely because no amendment, restatement, or modification has occurred.

The supplied source does not resolve the referenced 'even date herewith,' the identity/definition of Owner, or the actual agreement and its amendments. Those listed dependencies are absent, so the source is insufficient to verify application to an actual instrument.

c11 and c12 each describe two separate agreements but encode only the first agreement in a single-document fact vector. The vector does not represent all material facts in the case text and does not specify the document/scope being classified.
The rule summary's 'if and only if' formulation overstates the source: the quoted language is a definition by reference to a particular agreement, not a five-factor eligibility test.

The source defines an Enterprise as a legal entity together with subsidiaries that the legal entity owns by more than 50 percent. It does not require every qualifying entity to itself own a subsidiary by more than 50 percent.

The proposed predicate improperly makes ownership of a greater-than-50-percent subsidiary a necessary condition. Under the source, a qualifying subsidiary may be part of the Enterprise even though it owns no subsidiary itself.
The case schema lacks a fact establishing whether the named entity is a qualifying subsidiary owned by a legal entity by more than 50 percent, so it cannot represent the source definition exactly.

The United States language limits application of the term to the physically located portion of an Enterprise; it is not stated as a separate entity-level eligibility condition in the manner modeled by the predicate.

The quoted definition requires 'treatment' but does not define treatment or state that palliation and supportive care are categorically outside treatment. The program's explicit exclusion of those categories is therefore an unsupported narrowing, not an exact reflection of the quoted rule.

The stated source dependencies acknowledge that application depends on an external meaning of 'treatment,' but no such controlling definition or attachment is supplied. The quote alone cannot establish the proposed categorical boundaries among treatment, palliation, and supportive care.

The claimed therapeutic agent/product-context dependency is not present in the quoted definition. It should not be treated as a source requirement unless additional contract language defining Indication in relation to a Product is provided.
Each case's coded fields are explicitly supported by its fact text; the defect is the unsupported rule-level interpretation rather than a mismatch between case text and fact vectors.

The source defines a Contract Year as a twelve-month period commencing on each January 1 'throughout the Contract Period'; it does not expressly require that the entire twelve-month period be fully contained within the Contract Period. The predicate adds the unsupported condition period_fully_within_contract_period=true.

The proposed treatment would exclude a January 1 twelve-month period when the Contract Period ends during that period (for example, the early-termination case), but the quoted definition does not state that result.

The definition of 'Contract Period,' including the effect of 'unless sooner terminated,' is identified as a dependency but is not supplied in the source quote. That external definition is necessary to determine the intended scope of 'throughout the Contract Period' and any termination exception.
The case texts explicitly provide the dates and containment/termination assertions used by their coded fact vectors; no individual case has a redacted or unstated coded fact.

The predicate omits the express source requirement that the Regulatory Authority be 'applicable.' No applicability field or case fact is supplied, and necessity does not exactly establish applicability.

The predicate adds an unsupported requirement that the regulatory jurisdiction itself be national, regional, state, or local. The source applies those modifiers to a regulatory agency, not to the phrase 'regulatory jurisdiction.'

The independent is_governmental=true requirement is not an exact restatement of the list. The source says 'agency, department, bureau, commission, council or other governmental entity'; 'governmental' expressly modifies the residual 'other ... entity,' not necessarily every enumerated category as a separate Boolean condition.

The program does not establish that necessity is for the specified activity concerning the pharmaceutical product in the relevant regulatory jurisdiction; separate scalar fields do not encode that relational linkage.
The source does not define 'pharmaceutical product' or 'regulatory jurisdiction,' and no external definitions or jurisdictional/applicability evidence is attached.
Every case lacks an explicit coded fact establishing that the named entity is applicable in the relevant regulatory jurisdiction, despite applicability being required by the source.
c17 is internally inconsistent: its text says the entity is necessary for development, then says the activity is none of the listed activities; the fact vector codes activity as none_of_these.
c18 is internally inconsistent: its text first says the entity is necessary for development and then says necessity is false; the fact vector selects false without resolving the contradiction.
c19 is internally inconsistent: its text calls the entity a national regulatory agency but then states that its entity type is an individual person.
c20 is internally inconsistent: its text calls the entity a national regulatory agency but then states that its entity type is a private company.

The definition of 'relevant Regulatory Authority' is not supplied. Accordingly, the statement that a trade association is not the relevant Regulatory Authority is not established by the case text or source excerpt.

The 'multiple unspecified regions' wording does not expressly establish that the approval is not necessary in a particular country or jurisdiction; it could encompass one or more particular jurisdictions. The coded jurisdiction_scope value 'other' is therefore unsupported.
The definitions of 'Regulatory Authority' and 'Product' are required external dependencies but are absent, so the source excerpt cannot fully resolve those referenced terms.

Subject to the missing incorporated definitions, the predicate tracks the enumerated instrument types, authority requirement, necessity requirement, listed activities, Product limitation, and country-or-jurisdiction limitation.

The definition identifies 'that certain' agreement; the proposed predicate converts this into a generic if-and-only-if test based only on agreement type, entity, date, and a binary amendment flag. It does not preserve the identity/reference function of 'that certain.'

'(As amended)' is treated as an independent requirement that the document 'has been amended.' The quoted definition does not establish that any historical or asserted amendment, regardless of validity, effectiveness, execution, or legal status, qualifies the document as the defined agreement.

Cases c08-c15 expressly introduce material amendment-status qualifications (side letter, amended and restated, invalid, not effective, proposed, oral, unsigned, and disputed), but collapse each into as_amended=true. The source supplies no basis for treating those qualifications as legally operative amendments, and the fact vectors omit the distinctions necessary to do so.

The original Limited Partnership Agreement, its preamble identifying Moelis Holdings, and the relevant amendment instruments are absent. Those missing dependencies are needed to identify the referenced agreement and determine what constitutes part of it 'as amended.'
The source quote alone does not support the proposed iff formulation or resolution of the amendment edge cases.

The source does not make being a successor or assign of the specified entity an independent Affiliate criterion. 'Or its successors or assigns' modifies the specified person or entity with which the candidate must have a control relationship. The predicate's independent successor_or_assign_of_specified_entity arm is therefore erroneous; c11 is not established as an Affiliate on the stated facts.

The ownership rule is 'more than fifty percent (50%)' on a fully diluted basis. The predicate instead enumerates four particular percentages (50.1, 60, 75, and 100), so it fails for other qualifying percentages, such as 51% or 55%. It is not an exact implementation of a greater-than-50 test.

The source's management-and-policies limb applies where the candidate has the stated right 'whether by contract or otherwise.' The predicate improperly requires a separate right_by_contract_or_otherwise fact in addition to the right itself. That phrase describes permissible bases for the right rather than an additional limiting element. c14 demonstrates the resulting exclusion.

Most case vectors code numerous false facts that their texts do not expressly negate. For example, c01 states direct control but does not expressly establish absence of indirect control, ownership, voting rights, management rights, common control, or successor/assign status. The same unsupported-negative-fact problem affects c01-c15. c16 is the only case that broadly and expressly negates the relevant relationships.

c14 is internally problematic as phrased: a right that is 'not by contract or otherwise' is not a coherent negation of a source clause that expressly covers contract and all other bases. In any event, the program's additional mechanism requirement is not faithful to the definition.
The single-valued entity field cannot represent the source's express 'IMPCO, MIL and/or MINDA' formulation where more than one named Party may apply.
Cases c04-c06 explicitly state two named entities, but each fact vector codes only one entity and omits the other stated entity.
Because the predicate is evaluated over a mutually exclusive single entity value, it does not exactly model cases in which IMPCO, MIL, and/or MINDA jointly apply.

The predicate does not represent the express inclusion of the defined term "Sponsor Advertising Content." Treating it merely as an example of already-proprietary delivered content is a plausible gloss, but the source does not state that Sponsor Advertising Content is necessarily proprietary or otherwise collapsible into the proprietary_content field.

The definition or operative facts for the capitalized dependency "Sponsor Advertising Content" are absent. Without that attachment, it cannot be determined whether it creates an independent included category or how it relates to the proprietary-content requirement.
All supplied case narratives explicitly support their coded Boolean facts, but none tests the stated Sponsor Advertising Content inclusion.
